newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds fail to get into gear.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds fail to get into gear.

text.p: *Australian bonds succumbed to a fairly drab session after an initial U.S.-led mark down as the market bided its time ahead of Thursday's key labour force report for August.
Australian bonds succumbed to a fairly drab session after an initial U.S.-led mark down as the market bided its time ahead of Thursday's key labour force report for August, traders said.
"There's been a little bit of offshore selling, but mainly its all been in the rollover. It's been a fairly boring episode," one trader said.
Futures rollover activity ahead of the September bond expires on Monday again bolstered otherwise thin turnover.
Interest should pick up on Thursday with the jobs report and RBA officials testifying to a parliamentary banking committee.
Both outgoing governor Bernie Fraser and incoming governor Ian Macfarlane will face the committee.
Median forecasts for Australian employment centre on a 12,000 increase compared with a 9,800 increase in July, according to a Reuter survey of economists.
Employment could get a boost of between 10,000 and 15,000 from the hiring of census collectors in August.

The unemployment rate is seen holding at 8.5 percent on average, although some economists see it rising to 8.7 percent, a level which could see the market again speculating on a near-term cut in official interest rates, traders said.

The local 10-year bond yield spread to the U.S. seesawed around 120 basis points for most of the day. U.S. bonds ended a two day run of gains after a Fed official said that the economy was entering into an "inflationary danger zone", fuelling worries of a tightening when the FOMC meets on September 24.
